question.problem:
A triangle has sides $x$, $y$, and $z.$ The sides $x$, $y$, and $z$ are of lengths  $8$, $15$, and $17$, respectively. In degrees, what is the measure of the angle $X$ between the sides $y$ and $z?$ Round your answer to the **nearest tenth of a degree**.

$m∠X≈$
{{field-1}} ${}^{∘}$
question.worked_solution:
The following triangle illustrates the information given.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/linear/14269732/assets/db40512e5f82f1625602c6e8a350ebcf49c2d85596ae89e71b869a50f895315c.png)

We use the Law of Cosines to solve for angle $A:$

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡X & =\frac{{y}^{2}+{z}^{2}-{x}^{2}}{2yz}.\end{aligned}
$$

 

Here, we have

$$
x=8,\,y=15,\,z=17.
$$

This gives 

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡X & =\frac{{15}^{2}+{17}^{2}-{8}^{2}}{2(15)(17)} \\  & =\frac{225+289-64}{510} \\  & =\frac{450}{510} \\  & =\frac{15}{17}.\end{aligned}
$$

 
Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}m∠X & =\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{15}{17}) \\  & ≈{28.1}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

rounded to the nearest tenth.
